title: Java Hello World and Basics
content:
public class HelloWorld {                              // class define karo
    public static void main(String[] args) {   // entry point — JVM starts here
        // ── Print statements ──────────────────────────────────
        System.out.println("Hello, World!");     // println = print + newline
        System.out.println("Welcome to QueryNest!");   // output print karo

        // ── Variable declaration (must specify type in Java) ──
        int     age    = 20;     // integer — whole numbers only
        double  marks  = 92.5;   // double — decimal numbers (64-bit precision)
        float   pi     = 3.14f;  // float — decimal (32-bit, needs 'f' suffix)
        String  name   = "Alice"; // String — text (capital S, it's an object)
        boolean active = true;    // boolean — only true or false
        char    grade  = 'A';     // char — single character in single quotes

        // ── Formatted output ─────────────────────────────────
        System.out.println("Name: " + name);    // string concatenation with +
        System.out.printf("Marks: %.2f%n", marks); // printf: %.2f = 2 decimal places, %n = newline

        // ── Type casting ──────────────────────────────────────
        int x = (int) marks;     // double → int (truncates decimal, cast needed)
        double y = age;          // int → double (automatic, no cast needed)
        System.out.println("Cast: " + x + ", Auto: " + y); // output print karo
    }
}

Java String Methods
content:
public class StringMethods {                           // class define karo
    public static void main(String[] args) {           // main method — program yahan se shuru hota hai
        String s = "Hello, QueryNest!";                // String variable

        System.out.println(s.length());             // 17
        System.out.println(s.toUpperCase());        // HELLO, QUERYNEST!
        System.out.println(s.toLowerCase());        // hello, querynest!
        System.out.println(s.replace("Hello","Hi")); // Hi, QueryNest!
        System.out.println(s.contains("Query"));    // true
        System.out.println(s.startsWith("Hello"));  // true
        System.out.println(s.endsWith("!"));         // true
        System.out.println(s.indexOf("Q"));          // 7
        System.out.println(s.substring(7));          // QueryNest!
        System.out.println(s.substring(7, 12));      // Query
        System.out.println(s.trim());                // no leading/trailing spaces
        System.out.println(s.charAt(0));             // H

        // Split
        String csv = "Alice,20,Mumbai,92.5";           // String variable
        String[] parts = csv.split(",");
        for (String p : parts) System.out.println(p);  // output print karo

        // StringBuilder (efficient)
        StringBuilder sb = new StringBuilder();        // object banao
        for (int i = 1; i <= 5; i++) sb.append(i).append(" "); // integer variable
        System.out.println(sb.toString().trim()); // 1 2 3 4 5

        // Compare
        String a = "hello", b = "HELLO";               // String variable
        System.out.println(a.equals(b));           // false
        System.out.println(a.equalsIgnoreCase(b)); // true
        System.out.println(a.compareTo("world")); // negative
    }
}

title: Java ArrayList and Collections
content:
import java.util.*;

public class ListDemo {                                // class define karo
    public static void main(String[] args) {           // main method — program yahan se shuru hota hai
        // ArrayList
        ArrayList<String> students = new ArrayList<>(); // object banao
        students.add("Alice");                         // list mein add karo
        students.add("Bob");                           // list mein add karo
        students.add("Charlie");                       // list mein add karo
        students.add(1, "Dave");    // insert at index 1

        System.out.println(students);           // [Alice, Dave, Bob, Charlie]
        System.out.println(students.get(0));    // Alice
        System.out.println(students.size());    // 4
        System.out.println(students.contains("Bob")); // true
        System.out.println(students.indexOf("Bob"));  // 2

        students.remove("Bob");                 // remove by value
        students.remove(0);                    // remove by index
        students.set(0, "David");              // update

        Collections.sort(students);            // sort alphabetically
        Collections.reverse(students);         // reverse
        Collections.shuffle(students);         // shuffle

        // Iterate
        for (String s : students) System.out.print(s + " "); // output print karo
        System.out.println();                          // output print karo

        // LinkedList
        LinkedList<Integer> ll = new LinkedList<>();   // object banao
        ll.addFirst(10); ll.addLast(20); ll.add(30);   // list mein add karo
        System.out.println("First: " + ll.getFirst()); // output print karo
        System.out.println("Last:  " + ll.getLast());  // output print karo
        ll.removeFirst(); ll.removeLast();
    }
}

title: Java HashMap
content:
import java.util.*;

public class MapDemo {                                 // class define karo
    public static void main(String[] args) {           // main method — program yahan se shuru hota hai
        // HashMap — unordered
        HashMap<String, Integer> marks = new HashMap<>(); // object banao
        marks.put("Alice",   92);                      // map mein daalo
        marks.put("Bob",     78);                      // map mein daalo
        marks.put("Charlie", 85);                      // map mein daalo

        System.out.println(marks.get("Alice"));         // 92
        System.out.println(marks.getOrDefault("Eve", 0)); // 0
        System.out.println(marks.containsKey("Bob"));   // true
        System.out.println(marks.containsValue(85));    // true
        System.out.println(marks.size());               // 3

        marks.put("Alice", 97);       // update
        marks.remove("Bob");           // delete
        marks.putIfAbsent("Diana", 88); // add only if absent

        // Iterate
        for (Map.Entry<String,Integer> e : marks.entrySet()) // loop — repeat karo
            System.out.println(e.getKey() + " -> " + e.getValue()); // output print karo

        System.out.println("Keys:   " + marks.keySet()); // output print karo
        System.out.println("Values: " + marks.values()); // output print karo

        // TreeMap — sorted by key
        TreeMap<String,Integer> tm = new TreeMap<>(marks); // object banao
        System.out.println("First: " + tm.firstKey()); // output print karo
        System.out.println("Last:  " + tm.lastKey());  // output print karo

        // Frequency map (count occurrences)
        String[] words = {"apple","banana","apple","cherry","banana","apple"};
        HashMap<String,Integer> freq = new HashMap<>(); // object banao
        for (String w : words)                         // loop — repeat karo
            freq.put(w, freq.getOrDefault(w, 0) + 1);  // map mein daalo
        System.out.println("Frequency: " + freq);      // output print karo
    }
}

Java Number to Words
content:
public class NumberToWords {                           // class define karo
    static final String[] ones = {"","one","two","three","four","five","six","seven","eight","nine", // class level — object ki zaroorat nahi
        "ten","eleven","twelve","thirteen","fourteen","fifteen","sixteen","seventeen","eighteen","nineteen"};
    static final String[] tens = {"","","twenty","thirty","forty","fifty","sixty","seventy","eighty","ninety"}; // class level — object ki zaroorat nahi

    static String convert(int n) {                     // class level — object ki zaroorat nahi
        if (n == 0) return "zero";                     // condition check karo
        if (n < 20) return ones[n];                    // condition check karo
        if (n < 100) return tens[n/10] + (n%10 != 0 ? " " + ones[n%10] : ""); // condition check karo
        return ones[n/100] + " hundred" + (n%100 != 0 ? " " + convert(n%100) : ""); // value return karo
    }
    public static void main(String[] args) {           // main method — program yahan se shuru hota hai
        System.out.println(convert(0));   // zero
        System.out.println(convert(15));  // fifteen
        System.out.println(convert(99));  // ninety nine
        System.out.println(convert(100)); // one hundred
        System.out.println(convert(256)); // two hundred fifty six
    }
}

content:
import java.util.*;

public class RomanToInteger {                          // class define karo
    static int romanToInt(String s) {                  // class level — object ki zaroorat nahi
        Map<Character, Integer> map = new HashMap<>(); // object banao
        map.put('I',1); map.put('V',5); map.put('X',10); map.put('L',50); // map mein daalo
        map.put('C',100); map.put('D',500); map.put('M',1000); // map mein daalo
        int result = 0;                                // integer variable
        for (int i = 0; i < s.length(); i++) {         // integer variable
            int curr = map.get(s.charAt(i));           // integer variable
            int next = (i + 1 < s.length()) ? map.get(s.charAt(i + 1)) : 0; // integer variable
            if (curr < next) result -= curr;           // condition check karo
            else result += curr;                       // jab condition False ho
        }
        return result;                                 // value return karo
    }
    public static void main(String[] args) {           // main method — program yahan se shuru hota hai
        System.out.println(romanToInt("III"));   // 3
        System.out.println(romanToInt("IV"));    // 4
        System.out.println(romanToInt("IX"));    // 9
        System.out.println(romanToInt("LVIII")); // 58
        System.out.println(romanToInt("MCMXCIV")); // 1994
    }
}

title: Java Star Pyramid Pattern
Java Count Vowels Consonants
content:
public class VowelConsonant {                          // class define karo
    public static void main(String[] args) {           // main method — program yahan se shuru hota hai
        String str = "Hello World Java Programming";   // String variable
        int vowels = 0, consonants = 0, others = 0;    // integer variable
        for (char c : str.toLowerCase().toCharArray()) { // loop — repeat karo
            if ("aeiou".indexOf(c) != -1) vowels++;    // condition check karo
            else if (c >= 'a' && c <= 'z') consonants++; // condition check karo
            else others++;                             // jab condition False ho
        }
        System.out.println("Vowels: " + vowels);       // output print karo
        System.out.println("Consonants: " + consonants); // output print karo
        System.out.println("Others (spaces/digits): " + others); // output print karo
    }
}
